method.title: Method and limitations
method.howTitle: How the numbers are worked out
method.how1: Each shop gets one price per item each month: the middle of its prices that month (the median). A shop that reports every day doesn't outweigh one that reports weekly.
method.how2: An item's typical price is the middle of those shop prices, across all the shops in {state} or in one district.
method.how3: The basket cost adds up the typical prices of the 15 items, one of each.
method.how4: A price only counts when at least {min} shops priced the item, so a single shop can't set a district's price. That's why some districts have gaps.
method.how5: Totals are worked out exactly and rounded to the sen at the end, with half a sen rounding up.
method.limit1: PriceCatcher is collected to monitor prices. DOSM says it should complement the official CPI, not replace it, so this site shows basket costs, not an inflation rate.
method.limit2: Prices come from the shops that reported each month, and that set of shops changes over time.
method.limit3: District costs only appear in months when every item had at least {min} shops in that district, so smaller districts have gaps.
method.limit4: Fresh produce swings a lot from month to month, so compare trends rather than two single months.
method.limit5: The current month is partial until it ends.
method.limit6: Item names are shortened from PriceCatcher's official names. Petaling Jaya is listed separately from Petaling district, as it is in PriceCatcher.
method.qualityIntro: Since {month}, PriceCatcher has published {rows} prices across Malaysia. Before adding anything up, this site drops:

method.duplicates: It also counts {n} repeated rows (same day, shop and item), which are kept.
